title: Bilateral discordance of repeated grip change does not establish added digit-symbol prediction across NHANES samples
abstract: A fixed ridge model trained in 1,245 NHANES 2011–2012 adults aged 60+ was tested without refitting in 1,397 adults from the separate 2013–2014 sample. Adding the normalized absolute between-hand difference of first-to-third grip changes to peak strength, asymmetry, mean change, within-hand CV and demographic covariates reduced unweighted digit-symbol substitution MSE by 0.3107 score-squared (conditional stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval −0.2627 to 0.9357; joint training/target interval −0.3124 to 1.0934). The prespecified benefit criterion failed. Survey-weighted and pain-free standing sensitivities reversed the gain. Separate cross-sectional survey samples share infrastructure and do not establish independent-source transfer. Previously used grip caches make confirmation outcome-untouched rather than fully data-naive. No causal, diagnostic or clinical utility claim is made. Author algebraic checks and a byte-identical offline rerun are provided.
